question: Should Telegram expose standalone `pin` and `unpin` message-tool actions, and what gate/default plus target semantics should protect them?
rationale: The missing source surface is clear, but this feature gives agents privileged persistent chat-state mutation power through bot credentials and may require a new Telegram action gate plus explicit no-implicit-unpin semantics.

options.title: Approve gated explicit actions
options.body: Add Telegram-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind an explicit gate, require `messageId` for both actions unless separately approved, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Keep delivery pin only
options.body: Decline standalone pin/unpin for now and keep the existing `delivery.pin` capability for messages OpenClaw sends itself.

options.title: Request a design note first
options.body: Ask for a short design covering admin-right expectations, per-account gating, implicit unpin behavior, forum-topic semantics, and live-proof requirements before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve gated explicit actions
recommendation.body: Add Telegram-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind an explicit gate, require `messageId` for both actions unless separately approved, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their Telegram message-tool discovery and action-runtime commits are the strongest direct history for the contract this feature would extend.
